A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TFM-Token research, despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on four EEG datasets, tokenizer analyses, LaBraM integration experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds multi-dataset pretraining, ear-EEG evaluation, cross-dataset transfer, model integration results, and a downstream depth ablation.

M1.justification: The dual-path tokenizer, vector quantization, masking objectives, and downstream Transformer pipeline are retained. v2 Section 4.3 adds a BIOT adaptation that replaces raw EEG inputs with token embeddings while following BIOT's training protocol, alongside the existing LaBraM tokenizer substitution.

E1.justification: The four original datasets remain, and v2 adds EESM23 ear-EEG sleep staging. This introduces a different task, population, recording device, and four-channel ear configuration beyond the original scalp-EEG evaluations. Cross-dataset transfer scenarios also explicitly evaluate deployment of a tokenizer outside its training dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds EEGPT comparisons on all four original benchmarks, NeuroLM-B on TUEV and TUAB, and a distinct Vanilla BIOT variant. The pretrained BIOT comparator from v1 is retained as BIOT-star, rather than newly introduced. The tokenizer integration study also adds BIOT alongside LaBraM.

E3.justification: v1 uses single-dataset pretraining and fine-tuning; v2 adds four-dataset pretraining and transfer protocols varying whether masked-token pretraining occurs on the source or target dataset. EESM23 introduces 30-second epochs and subject splits 1–6/7–8/9–10. v2 also reports adopting published scores for several baselines, changing the comparison procedure, although Appendix B.5 retains an inconsistent blanket reproduction statement.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds transfer experiments separating tokenizer transfer from downstream pretraining transfer, and C.7 tests downstream depths of 1, 2, 4, 6, and 12 layers. Integration analyses expand to BIOT and additional settings. Existing masking, vocabulary, positional-embedding, and masked-token-pretraining ablations remain; v1 Figure 1's qualitative reconstruction comparison is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and means with standard deviations. v2 newly reports p-values for the multi-dataset IIIC comparison and ear-EEG evaluation, but does not identify the statistical tests. There is no stated increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Original single-dataset TFM scores remain unchanged, while substantial new result sets cover multi-dataset training, ear-EEG, transfer, integration, and depth. For example, TUEV Kappa 0.6189 is newly reported under multi-dataset training, rather than a same-setting revision of 0.5337. Some baseline entries are replaced, including SPaRCNet TUAB AUC-PR changing from 0.8782 to 0.8414. The earlier TUAB LaBraM-tokenizer substitution results are omitted.

T1.justification: The problem formulations and STFT mathematics move from v1 Section 3 to v2 Appendix A. The explicit nearest-neighbor quantization equation explains the existing VQ procedure. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: v2 shifts the contribution emphasis from the named tokenizer–encoder framework toward a reusable, model-agnostic tokenizer. It adds explicit first-work positioning for single-channel time-frequency motif tokenization and headline claims about multi-dataset performance, integration with both BIOT and LaBraM, and demonstrated cross-device ear-EEG scalability.

C2.justification: v2 adds physiological interpretation of the PLED examples, interprets retrieval as token consistency with possible contrastive-learning applications, and discusses transfer and shallow downstream models. The central explanations about joint frequency–temporal modeling and the limitation caused by motifs crossing fixed windows are retained.

D1.justification: Unlike v1, v2 provides project access instructions and a reproducibility statement reporting source code, pretrained weights, and preprocessing/loading/training scripts. It also documents ear-EEG filtering, cropping, corrupted-segment removal, splits, and additional baseline provenance. Core architecture and optimization tables remain unchanged. Resource availability is reported by the PDF and was not externally verified.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially repositioned around reusable EEG tokenization and motif learning. v2 introduces Motiflets, statistical tokenization literature, EEGPT, NeuroLM, and ear-EEG research, while removing the earlier standalone self-supervised representation-learning survey and several associated citations. Its explicit priority claims also strengthen the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Preliminary mathematics moves to the appendix, TFM-Encoder becomes a generic downstream Transformer in the main narrative, and experiments are reorganized around new questions. Reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column review format. v2 replaces the opening figure, reorganizes the framework diagram, redraws and splits token-quality plots, and redisplays input ablations graphically. IIIC and CHB-MIT tables move into the main text, while new integration, transfer, ear-EEG, and depth displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The ear-EEG and cross-dataset experiments directly address v1's limited evidence for generalization, while BIOT integration tests reuse beyond LaBraM and the access information strengthens reproducibility documentation. These are substantial gains supporting central contributions. Reporting weaknesses remain: Table 2 contradicts universal baseline dominance on multi-dataset CHB-MIT balanced accuracy, and Table 9 shows improvement in 31 of 36 comparisons, rather than the claimed 93%. These overstatements require correction but do not outweigh the added evidence.
